fit: oral red-perilla extract and nocturnal void frequency in healthy men
assessment: Fourteen healthy men reported 0.24 fewer nighttime voids per night on the extract versus starch (p<.05). Daytime void frequency was inconclusive. Urgency, Parkinson status and fresh-leaf consumption were outside the comparison.

fit: mixed ginger and perilla extract dyspepsia registry with inconsistent problem label
assessment: The title, arms and outcomes register gastrointestinal symptoms. The condition field labels dysphonia. No vocal-intensity endpoint, dried culinary shiso exposure, or posted results.

fit: cayenne capsules and electronically measured maximal sprint speed
assessment: Nineteen healthy athletes showed similar fastest and average repeated sprint times during commercial cayenne and placebo. Combined gastrointestinal symptoms increased. No ordinary walking assessment or Parkinson sample.

fit: dissolved powdered ginger and resting pressure in older women
assessment: Hypertensive water and ginger groups showed comparable resting systolic changes of −2.70 and −3.28 mmHg. No standing challenge, Parkinson cohort or fresh-grated ginger.

fit: black pepper oil odor and whole saliva secretion
assessment: The author abstract reports higher saliva output after black pepper oil odor. Sixty healthy students were randomized to oil odors or water. The complete tables, clinical drooling and culinary ingestion remain outside the verified result.

fit: topical sesame oil and eight-meter walk in knee osteoarthritis
assessment: Noninferiority to diclofenac was reported for walk time. The abstract lacks the walk means, interval and margin. Topical treatment of knee osteoarthritis leaves effects of cold-pressed dietary oil on Parkinson gait open.

fit: oral sesame seeds and Timed Up and Go in knee osteoarthritis
assessment: Timed Up and Go improved in each group, with post-treatment difference p=.002. The abstract gives no group-specific times. Exposure was seed with standard care.

fit: injected sesame oil comparator in a planned mobility assessment
assessment: The registered critical-care study uses intramuscular oil as the testosterone comparator and plans Timed Up and Go. No posted outcome or oral cold-pressed oil.

fit: same Parkinson rectal sesame-oil cohort across two publications
assessment: The congress item republishes the 15-person rectal formulation comparison. Combined botanical and sesame oil exposures and MDS-UPDRS components provide no separate walking estimate.
